newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: COLOMBIA WATCHDOG ORDERS INQUIRY INTO NICKEL SALE.
newsitem.headline: COLOMBIA WATCHDOG ORDERS INQUIRY INTO NICKEL SALE.

text.p: Colombia's public sector watchdog ordered a formal inquiry Tuesday into alleged corruption in the sale of the government stake in the Cerro Matoso nickel mine to a unit of South African company Gencor.

Comptroller General David Turbay said he had detected "several irregularities" in the February 18 sale of the 47.7 percent stake in the mine -- the fourth largest of its kind in the world -- which it said led to the State losing an estimated $73.6 million in income.

Speaking in a press conference, Turbay did not directly attribute blame but implied the main fault lay with the Finance Ministry and the state-sponsored Institute for Industrial Promotion for undervaluing the shares and setting restrictive post-purchase conditions.
The investigation will be carried out by the Chief Prosecutor's Office and those officials found guilty of mishandling the privatization could face jail or personal fines.

Gencor previously owned just over half Cerro Matoso, in northwest Cordoba province, and purchased the government stake through its Colombian unit Billiton BVI Ltd. It now owns 98.9 percent of the mine with the remainder held by employees.
Turbay said Gencor paid $182.7 million but said the stake should have fetched at least $256 million.
The evaluation of the share package was carried out by Swiss Bank and Colombian finance company Corfigan, a unit of the Banco Ganadero, more than a year before the sale, he said.

Turbay added that the statutes of the state-run company at Cerro Matoso were revised shortly before its sell-off which would have restricted the amount of nickel a new partner in the operation would have been able to sell in the first five years after purchase.
This, Turbay said, discouraged 35 companies which had shown initial interest in purchasing the government stake. In the event the sole bid was placed by Billiton.
The mine produced about 50 million tonnes of high-grade nickel in 1996.
